source.title: Cognitive control over learning: creating, clustering, and generalizing task-set structure.

confidence_rationale: The Context-Task-Set (C-TS) model is a direct prior-art analog of MECH-349's CREATE face: a nonparametric-Bayesian-inspired (Chinese Restaurant Process) mechanism that, on encountering a new context, decides to CREATE a new task-set structure rather than reuse an existing one, with the create-vs-reuse decision governed by a concentration parameter (alpha) exactly analogous in role to MECH-349's crf_mint_recurrence_threshold. This establishes the general phenomenon (discrete creation of new structural slots triggered by insufficient existing coverage of a recurring regularity) as pre-existing, tested computational and behavioral science, not a novel discovery. Confidence held at 0.6 rather than higher because the trigger mechanics differ: C-TS creation is a probabilistic draw from a CRP prior weighed against existing cluster popularity, updated via Bayesian posterior tracking, whereas MECH-349's mint is a deterministic recurrence-COUNT threshold with a hard context-match gate and a free-slot precondition -- closer to a rule-based trigger than a Bayesian nonparametric one, and MECH-349's specific churn/retirement dynamics (crf_maintenance_decay-driven selective retirement, tested by V3-EXQ-1025) have no counterpart in C-TS, which does not model retirement of existing task-sets at all.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The C-TS model treats task-set structure as generated by a Chinese Restaurant Process: for a new context c_{n+1}, P(TS = new | c_{n+1}) = alpha / A while P(TS = i | c_{n+1}) = N_i / A, where N_i is the popularity of existing task-set i and A = alpha + sum(N_i). 'For each new context, the probability of creating a new task-set is proportional to alpha, and the probability of reusing one of the known task-sets is proportional to the popularity of that task-set.' The model is validated behaviorally: humans 'spontaneously build task-set structure into a learning problem when not cued to do so,' and simulated agents were 'more likely to create a new task-set' when existing structure could not explain the current context-action contingency.
mapping.ree_translation: Directly analogous to MECH-349's CandidateRuleField._maybe_mint: both are structure-learning mechanisms that must decide, on encountering a context, whether to CREATE a new discrete structural slot (a task-set / a CandidateRule) or reuse/apply an existing one, with the decision governed by a single scalar control parameter (CRP's alpha; REE's crf_mint_recurrence_threshold) that trades off proliferation of new structure against reuse of existing structure. Both frame this as the mechanism that supplies structure gradient descent over a fixed representation cannot supply on its own.
mapping.mapping_caveat: C-TS's creation event is a probabilistic Bayesian draw re-evaluated online against a posterior over ALL existing task-sets' fit to the new context; MECH-349's mint is a hard-thresholded recurrence counter keyed to a specific (context-bucket, action-object) pair with a context-match gate, i.e. a rule-based trigger rather than a Bayesian nonparametric one. C-TS also has no analog to MECH-349's SELECTIVE CHURN/retirement question (whether a creator degrades gracefully when regularities go extinct) -- that half of MECH-349's empirical content (E2, tested by V3-EXQ-1025) is not addressed by this paper at all. Treat this as prior art for the CREATE face and the general create-vs-reuse tradeoff, not for the churn/retirement dynamics.
mapping.source_context: Computational model (C-TS) plus a neurobiologically explicit basal-ganglia/PFC network model, validated against human behavioral task-switching and generalization experiments (positive/negative transfer across contexts); no artificial-agent or REE-specific substrate.

confidence_components.notes: High source quality (canonical Psych Review paper combining a formal nonparametric-Bayesian model with a spiking/network implementation and human behavioral validation -- the closest thing to a direct ancestor of ARC-063/MECH-349 in the literature). Mapping fidelity moderate: the CREATE-vs-reuse tradeoff is a clean structural match; the specific trigger mechanics and the entire churn/retirement half of MECH-349 are not covered.
